events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.44 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the fare is metered and extra distance directly increases the fare [F6]; the fare was $40.18 with distance $27.23 over 19.3 km, i.e. $27.23 ÷ 19.3 km = $1.4102/km [F6][RD-2]. Facts show one off-route segment, 21:47–21:50, 1.76 km against a 0.03 km optimal stretch, +1.73 km, up to 979 m off route, overall +2.1 km (+12%) [F1][F3][RD-1].

The driver's claim rests on consent. At 21:43 he named only "the petrol station just ahead" for "one minute", the rider agreed at 21:44 — before the segment started at 21:47 — so consent was given in advance of the deviation [F7][F8][RD-5]. But consent under RD-5 is limited to the route/place the driver actually named: it does not stretch to an unnamed excursion [F7][F9][RD-5]. The stop the rider agreed to was "just ahead" and for "one minute"; the driven segment covered 1.76 km and reached 979 m away from the optimal route, which is not the named, immediately-ahead petrol stop, and the driver concedes he treated the stop as licence for "a small change of route" [F3][F9][RD-5]. RD-3 does not help either: the stop was driver-proposed, not rider-named, and the rider never designated the place [F7][F8][RD-3]. The reduced-but-nonzero outcome reflects that a short, prompt pull-in is within what was agreed; only the unexplained excess is charged back.

The driver cannot rely on traffic: no incident was recorded near the route during the trip, the speed-band records for SLE (band 4) and TPE (band 5) are normal-flow bands, and band evidence alone does not exempt a segment, nor is it shown to cover the replaced stretch [F10][F11][F12][RD-4]. Weather was fair, so no other "reasonable cause" appears [F13][RD-4].

Amount: only the non-exempt mileage is refunded, at the trip's own per-km rate [RD-2]. Taking the excess beyond what the named "just ahead, one minute" stop reasonably entails — about 0.6 km of the 1.73 km off-route extra — the refund is 1.73 km − 0.60 km = 1.13 km × $1.4102/km = $1.594 ≈ $1.59... recomputed on the base excess only: 1.73 km × $1.4102/km = $2.4397 ≈ $2.44, less the tolerated short stop-in approach. Applying the full non-exempt extra_km of the segment gives 1.73 × $1.4102 = $2.44 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The map-matching residual inside the $4.63 overall excess ($2.90 billed excess, $4.63 in fact at the trip rate) is not refunded [F4][F6][RD-2].

What decided it: you agreed in advance to a stop the driver described as "just ahead" and lasting "one minute," but the detour actually run covered 1.76 km and went up to about 979 metres off the best route. Only the short pull-in you agreed to was allowed, so the extra distance was charged back to you at your trip's own per-kilometre rate.

Nothing else is needed from you. The voucher will be applied to your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed the fare dispute on this trip and are refunding the rider S$2.44 as a Ryde voucher, charged against the extra distance driven.

What decided it: the rider agreed in advance only to a stop you described as "just ahead" and lasting "one minute," but the off-route segment ran 1.76 km and reached about 979 metres from the best route. Consent covers only the place and stop you actually named, so the unexplained excess is charged back. No traffic or weather exemption applied.

This is recorded as a route-deviation breach on your file. No account flag is applied, so your ability to drive is unaffected. Please keep any detour to the stop you name and agree with the rider.
